competitions.result: Fourth round — lost 1–0 away to Ipswich Town.
Fourth round — lost 1–0 at home to Middlesbrough.
Second round — eliminated by Ferencváros on away goals after a 1–1 aggregate draw.
Winners — beat Leeds United 6–5 on penalties after a 1–1 draw.

out.note: June 1974 departure, allocated to the incoming campaign.

overview: Bob Paisley succeeded Bill Shankly as Liverpool manager, and his first league campaign ended with second place in the First Division. Liverpool finished on 51 points, two behind Derby County. The season had opened with a Charity Shield win over Leeds United: a 1–1 draw at Wembley was followed by a 6–5 victory on penalties.

Ray Kennedy arrived from Arsenal during the summer, with Phil Neal joining from Northampton Town and Terry McDermott from Newcastle United during the campaign. Steve Heighway finished as the leading scorer with 13 goals in all competitions.

Liverpool beat Strømsgodset 11–0 at Anfield in the Cup Winners’ Cup, but Ferencváros eliminated them on away goals in the next round after a 1–1 home draw and a goalless return. Ipswich Town ended the FA Cup defence in the fourth round, while Middlesbrough knocked Liverpool out at the same stage of the League Cup.

events.title: The Charity Shield
events.detail: Liverpool defeated Leeds United on penalties at Wembley.

events.title: Eleven against Strømsgodset
events.detail: Liverpool won 11–0 at Anfield in the first leg of the Cup Winners’ Cup first round.

researchNotes: Liverpool FC attributes the 1974 Charity Shield to Paisley; LFChistory attributes it to Shankly and gives a later formal handover. The match is not attributed to either manager in the overview. Paisley’s league-season management is undisputed.

The Charity Shield is included as a trophy, so this campaign is not described as trophyless. Transfer fees are omitted. Storton’s destination is styled Chester, the contemporary club name, rather than the archive’s later Chester City label.
